import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def discrete_log_naive_precond (g h p : UInt64) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  p.toNat > 1
  -- !benchmark @end precond

def is_discrete_log (g h p : Nat) (x : Nat) : Prop :=
  (Nat.pow g x) % p = h % p

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
def findDLogAux (g h p : Nat) (i remaining : Nat) : Option Nat :=
  match remaining with
  | 0 => none
  | r + 1 =>
      if (Nat.pow g i) % p = h % p then
        some i
      else
        findDLogAux g h p (i + 1) r
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def discrete_log_naive (g h p : UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) : Option UInt64 :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  match findDLogAux g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat 0 p.toNat with
  | some x => some (UInt64.ofNat x)
  | none => none
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def discrete_log_naive_postcond (g h p : UInt64) (result : Option UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  match result with
  | some x => is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat x.toNat ∧ x.toNat < p.toNat ∧
               ∀ k : Nat, k < x.toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
  | none => ∀ k : Nat, k < p.toNat → ¬ is_discrete_log g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat k
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem findDLogAux_correct (g h p i remaining : Nat) :
    match findDLogAux g h p i remaining with
    | some x =>
        i ≤ x ∧
        x < i + remaining ∧
        is_discrete_log g h p x ∧
        ∀ k : Nat, i ≤ k → k < x → ¬ is_discrete_log g h p k
    | none =>
        ∀ k : Nat, i ≤ k → k < i + remaining → ¬ is_discrete_log g h p k := by
  induction remaining generalizing i with
  | zero =>
      simp [findDLogAux]
      intro k hik hk hlog
      omega
  | succ remaining ih =>
      simp only [findDLogAux]
      by_cases hi : (Nat.pow g i) % p = h % p
      · rw [if_pos hi]
        refine ⟨le_rfl, by omega, ?_, ?_⟩
        · unfold is_discrete_log
          exact hi
        · intro k hik hk hlog
          omega
      · rw [if_neg hi]
        cases hres : findDLogAux g h p (i + 1) remaining with
        | none =>
            have ihnone := ih (i + 1)
            rw [hres] at ihnone
            intro k hik hk hlog
            by_cases hki : k = i
            · subst k
              apply hi
              simpa [is_discrete_log] using hlog
            · exact ihnone k (by omega) (by omega) hlog
        | some x =>
            have ihsome := ih (i + 1)
            rw [hres] at ihsome
            rcases ihsome with ⟨hix, hxlt, hxlog, hmin⟩
            refine ⟨by omega, by omega, hxlog, ?_⟩
            intro k hik hk hlog
            by_cases hki : k = i
            · subst k
              apply hi
              simpa [is_discrete_log] using hlog
            · exact hmin k (by omega) hk hlog

theorem UInt64_ofNat_toNat_of_lt {n : Nat} (hn : n < UInt64.size) :
    (UInt64.ofNat n).toNat = n := by
  have hmod : n % UInt64.size = n := Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hn
  simpa [hmod]
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem discrete_log_naive_postcond_satisfied (g h p : UInt64) (h_precond : discrete_log_naive_precond g h p) :
    discrete_log_naive_postcond g h p (discrete_log_naive g h p h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  unfold discrete_log_naive
  have hc := findDLogAux_correct g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat 0 p.toNat
  cases hfind : findDLogAux g.toNat h.toNat p.toNat 0 p.toNat with
  | none =>
      rw [hfind] at hc
      dsimp [discrete_log_naive_postcond]
      intro k hk
      exact hc k (Nat.zero_le k) (by omega)
  | some x =>
      rw [hfind] at hc
      rcases hc with ⟨h0x, hxlt, hxlog, hmin⟩
      dsimp [discrete_log_naive_postcond]
      have hpSize : p.toNat < UInt64.size := UInt64.toNat_lt p
      have hxSize : x < UInt64.size := by omega
      have hxToNat : (UInt64.ofNat x).toNat = x :=
        UInt64_ofNat_toNat_of_lt hxSize
      rw [hxToNat]
      refine ⟨hxlog, by omega, ?_⟩
      intro k hk
      exact hmin k (Nat.zero_le k) hk
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Your task is to implement a solver for the Discrete Logarithm Problem and verify its correctness in Lean. Given a base g, a target h, and a modulus p, find the smallest non-negative integer x < p such that g^x ≡ h (mod p), or return none if no such x exists. Algorithm: Use a naive linear search. Iterate `x` from 0 to `p-1`. Maintain a running product for `g^x % p` to avoid recomputing the power from scratch. Minimality: If multiple solutions exist, you must return the smallest `x`. You must prove the invariant that at iteration `i`, `current_val == (Nat.pow g i) % p`. (2) Negative Proof (None): The hardest part is the `none` case. If the loop finishes without returning, you must prove the universal quantifier: `for all k < p, (Nat.pow g k) % p \ne h % p`. (3) Minimality (Some): When you return `some x`, you must prove that no earlier index `k < x` was a solution. Since your loop searches strictly from 0 upwards, this follows from the control flow, but you must capture it in the loop invariant ("for all checked k, g^k % p\ne h % p").
